articles.summary: A great blowout isn't just about technique. It's about working with your hair type, protecting your hair from heat, and creating a routine that builds smoothness, volume, and shine from the start. Whether your hair is straight, wavy, curly, or coily, understanding how heat changes your hair's structure can help you achieve longer-lasting results with less damage. Key Takeaways The best blowouts start with clean, conditioned hair that's matched to your hair type. Heat protection is essential for helping reduce moisture loss and protecting the hair cuticle. Drying your hair in sections creates smoother, longer-lasting results. Allowing each section to cool helps lock in shape and volume. Lightweight styling products help support movement, reduce frizz, and improve longevity without weighing hair down. Why Hair Prep Matters Your blowout starts long before you pick up a blow dryer. Healthy-looking blowouts begin with hair that's clean, hydrated, and conditioned for your hair type. Product buildup, excess oil, or dehydrated hair can all affect how your style looks and how long it lasts. Wash your hair with your Function of Beauty Custom Shampoo and Conditioner, personalized for your hair type and goals. If your goal is hydration, frizz control, or strengthening, your formula is designed to support those needs before styling even begins. After washing, gently squeeze excess water from your hair with a microfiber towel or cotton T-shirt instead of rubbing, which can create unnecessary friction and frizz. Step 1: Apply Your Styling Products The best time to apply styling products is while your hair is still damp. Choose products based on the result you want to achieve: Custom Styling Primer helps protect against heat while smoothing the hair and reducing frizz. Formulated with provitamin B5 that provides color, UV, and heat protection (up to 450°F). Formulated for your unique hair goals with a personalized level of hold. Size: 6 oz Custom Hair Serum at the ends adds lightweight hydration and shine while helping smooth the hair cuticle. Formulated with sunflower seed oil and jojoba oil that smooths frizz, enhances shine, and protect hair from heat. The lightweight formula is fit for all hair types. Size: 3 oz Zero Gravity Mousse provides flexible volume and body without making hair feel stiff. Mousse adds volume, structure, and hold to a blowout. When activated by the heat of a blow dryer, its polymers expand to plump each hair strand and create lift at the roots. Distribute products evenly from mid-lengths to ends, adding mousse closer to the roots if you're looking for extra lift. Step 2: Rough Dry First Instead of immediately reaching for a round brush, begin by rough drying your hair until it's about 70-80% dry. Use your fingers to lift the roots while directing airflow downward. This removes excess moisture, shortens styling time, and reduces the amount of heat your hair experiences overall. Step 3: Choose the Right Tools Your technique matters, but so do your tools. Always use a concentrator nozzle on your blow dryer. Focused airflow helps smooth the cuticle for a shinier finish while giving you better control. Choose your brush based on your styling goals: Large round brush: Creates volume and movement. Medium round brush: Adds body with soft bends. Paddle brush: Creates a sleek, smooth finish. Step 4: Work in Sections Divide your hair into manageable sections before styling. Working with smaller sections allows heat to reach each piece evenly while maintaining the tension needed for a smooth finish. Place your brush underneath each section and slowly pull through while following closely with your dryer. Keep the airflow moving from roots to ends to encourage the cuticle to lie flat. Continue until each section is completely dry before moving to the next. Step 5: Let Your Hair Cool Heat temporarily reshapes the hydrogen bonds inside your hair, but cooling is what helps set your style. After drying each section, leave it wrapped around the brush or pin it loosely for several seconds before releasing. This simple step helps improve volume, bounce, and longevity. Step 6: Finish Your Style Once your hair has completely cooled, finish with a few drops of Custom Hair Serum through the mid-lengths and ends for added shine and frizz control. If you want additional volume, gently lift your roots with your fingertips instead of adding more heat. Blowout Tips by Hair Type Straight Hair Use lightweight styling Zero Gravity Mousse in small amounts at the root to avoid weighing hair down and focus on creating lift at the roots for long-lasting volume. Wavy Hair Work in smaller sections to smooth the hair while preserving natural movement with your round brush after applying Zero Gravity Mousse at the root. Add Styling Primer to help minimize humidity-related frizz and hold your style. Curly Hair If you're creating a smooth blowout, allow curls to stretch gradually rather than forcing them straight in one pass. Working slowly helps reduce unnecessary heat exposure. Work in smaller sections to smooth the hair while preserving natural movement with your round brush after applying Zero Gravity Mousse at the root. Add Styling Primer to help minimize humidity-related frizz and hold your style. Coily Hair Begin with well-conditioned hair and use smaller sections with consistent tension. Taking your time creates smoother results while helping protect the hair's structure. Work in smaller sections to smooth the hair while preserving natural movement with your round brush after applying Zero Gravity Mousse at the root. Add Styling Primer to help minimize humidity-related frizz and hold your style. The Bottom Line A salon-worthy blowout isn't about using the highest heat or the most products. It's about understanding how your hair responds to moisture, heat, and styling. When you start with products personalized to your hair type and goals, protect your hair during styling, and use the right technique, you can create a smooth, voluminous blowout that lasts longer while helping keep your hair healthy over time.

articles.summary: Humidity season is here, and if your hair has its own opinion about the weather, you're not imagining it. Frizz isn't a flaw — it's physics. And once you understand what's actually happening at the strand level, you can stop fighting your hair type and start working with it. Frizz Is Structural, Not Random Here is the science: Hair is made primarily of keratin, a strong structural protein that naturally absorbs and releases water. On humid days, keratin draws moisture from the air into the hair shaft. As the hair absorbs that extra water, it swells, temporarily changing the hydrogen bonds that help determine your hair's shape. If moisture enters unevenly, the cuticle can lift, leading to frizz, puffiness, or a loss of definition. How much this happens depends on your hair's structure, which is why straight, wavy, curly, and coily hair each respond differently to humidity. That's also why a one-size-fits-all anti-frizz product rarely works for everyone in the room. Straight hair, wavy hair, curly hair, and coily hair each let moisture in and let it out differently, which means each one needs a different defense. As hair type experts, this is the exact problem we built Function of Beauty around: structure-matched care, not guesswork. How Frizz Shows Up by Hair Type Straight hair lies closest to the scalp, so it tends to pick up humidity fast and go flat or limp rather than visibly frizzy, though flyaways are still frizz's cousin. Straight hair's sebum (its natural oil) distributes easily down the shaft, which is great for shine but means it can look greasy before it looks frizzy. Wavy hair sits between straight and curly. It has more volume than straight hair but less natural definition than curly hair, which makes it prone to both frizz and a kind of directionless puff when humidity hits. Curly hair has a curled hair shaft that affects how oil travels from root to tip. That uneven oil distribution is why curls can look dry and frizzy at the same time. It can be one or the other, or both, for a structural reason. Coily hair has the tightest curl pattern and the most cuticle separation, making it both the most porous and the most fragile hair type. Sebum can't really navigate those tight coils. This leaves the hair chronically dry. When dry, the outer layer (cuticle) lifts, allowing humidity from the air to enter the shaft, causing the strands to swell and expand Matching Your Hair Routine to Your Hair Structure This is why we created our Hair Type Collections. Every shampoo and conditioner, leave-in treatment, and mask is formulated with the unique characteristics of straight, wavy, curly, and coily hair in mind, helping each hair type respond better to humidity with the moisture, lightweight care, or nourishment it needs. Straight Hair Shampoo & Conditioner, with coconut water and avocado oil, are built to cleanse and hydrate without weighing strands down — because straight hair doesn't need heavy moisture, it needs balance. Wavy Hair Shampoo & Conditioner, with fermented rice water and argan oil, target the smooth-and-strengthen combo wavy hair needs to hold its shape instead of frizzing into a halo. Curly Hair Shampoo & Conditioner, with flaxseed extract and Brazilian pracaxi oil, hydrate while gently cleansing, which helps curls stay defined instead of fighting both dryness and frizz at once. Coily Hair Shampoo & Conditioner, with chia seeds and Jamaican black castor oil, deliver the intensive moisture coily hair needs from root to tip, since it can't rely on its own sebum to do that work. If you're curly or coily, this is also a great season to lean on our Co-Wash. It's gentler than a full shampoo and lighter than a conditioner, so it won't strip the moisture your curls are working hard to hold onto. We recommend alternating it with your shampoo to keep your scalp clean without over-drying your strands. Twice a week, for any hair type dealing with humidity-related dryness, our Hair Mask gives you a deeper dose of conditioning with ingredients like shea butter, jojoba ester, and argan oil that go to work for 5 to 10 minutes to help reinforce the cuticle layer that humidity loves to disrupt. The Last Line of Defense: Sealing It All In Once your cleanse-and-condition routine is structure-matched, the final step is locking that moisture in before it has a chance to escape or before outside humidity has a chance to get in. For most hair types, that means a styling product that seals the cuticle rather than just sitting on top of it. If you've got a specific frizz-prone day ahead of you — a wedding, a humid vacation, a big presentation and want something built around your exact hair goals, our Custom Hair Serum is formulated to reduce frizz by 70% and protect against thermal damage up to 400°F, with your choice of hair goals layered in. It's a nice option to have in your back pocket for the days your regular routine needs backup. The Takeaway Frizz isn't a sign your hair care routine is failing; it's your hair's structure responding to its environment exactly the way it's built to. The fix isn't more product; it's the right product for your specific hair type. That's the whole idea behind Function of Beauty: we don't guess at what your hair needs. We start with the structure and build from there. Take the quiz, find your hair type collection, and let your hair do less work fighting the humidity this summer.

articles.summary: By late July, your hair has weathered weeks of sun, humidity, chlorine, salt water, and heat styling. The frizz, flatness, dryness, or breakage you're noticing isn't random—it's a reflection of what's happened to your hair's structure over time. Every strand responds differently based on its hair type, but the science is the same: summer gradually changes how your hair holds moisture, protects itself, and behaves. Here's what's happening beneath the surface, and what an effective late-summer reset actually looks like. Why Summer Is Structurally Demanding on Hair Hair behaves the way it does because of how it's built: a cortex (the inner protein structure that provides strength and elasticity), a cuticle (the overlapping outer layer that protects the strand), and a lipid layer that coats the surface and regulates moisture movement. Summer challenges all three parts of the hair structure. UV rays gradually break down proteins in the cortex while oxidizing the protective lipids on the surface. Chlorine strips away that lipid layer, leaving the cuticle rougher and more vulnerable to moisture loss. Humidity repeatedly forces water into and out of the hair, temporarily disrupting hydrogen bonds inside the cortex and causing the cuticle to lift, leading to frizz and loss of shape. Over weeks of sun, swimming, heat, and humidity, these effects compound. The result isn't damaged hair overnight—it's hair that feels drier, rougher, less defined, and harder to manage because its natural protective structure has been worn down. A late-summer reset isn't about reversing every day at the beach. It's about restoring moisture, smoothing the cuticle, and reinforcing your hair's natural barrier so it can perform the way it was designed to. Straight Hair: Buildup Is Your Main Issue Straight hair's round follicles create a smooth pathway for sebum to travel from the scalp to the ends. That efficient oil distribution keeps strands naturally conditioned, but in summer it also means sweat, sunscreen residue, and styling products become noticeable more quickly. As oil and environmental buildup spread across the hair shaft, straight hair can look flat, heavy, or greasy sooner than other hair types. The result: By late July, flat roots and dull mid-lengths usually aren't about dryness. They're about buildup sitting on a cuticle that's been lying flat the whole time. Your reset: Start with a thorough shampoo wash focused on the scalp — the Straight Hair Shampoo is formulated with coconut water to remove buildup without stripping the lightweight moisture balance straight hair needs. Follow with Straight Hair Conditioner (avocado oil, applied mid-lengths to ends only), and swap in the Straight Hair Mask once this week for a deeper treatment. The seaweed extract supports cuticle alignment, which is what gives straight hair its reflective quality when it's performing well. Wavy Hair: You're Fighting Two Things at Once Wavy hair's oval follicle creates its characteristic S-shaped pattern, making it harder for sebum to travel evenly from roots to ends. During summer, sweat, sunscreen, and styling products can build up more quickly at the roots, while the mid-lengths and ends receive less natural conditioning. The result: UV exposure gradually degrades the hair's protective lipid layer, and humidity repeatedly lifts the cuticle as moisture moves in and out of the strand. The result is hair that's oily at the roots, drier through the lengths, and more prone to frizz. Your reset: The Wavy Hair Shampoo handles the scalp without over-drying stressed ends. Use Wavy Hair Conditioner from mid-lengths down only. Mid-week, try a Co-Wash application instead of a second shampoo — it hydrates your lengths without adding to scalp buildup. Finish the week with the Wavy Hair Mask (vegan squalane) in place of conditioner for 10 minutes. For styling, scrunch Zero-Gravity Styling Mousse into soaking wet hair and let it air dry without touching. Curly Hair: Moisture Loss Is Structural, and Summer Makes It Worse Curly hair's spiral structure makes it difficult for sebum to travel from the scalp to the ends, leaving the mid-lengths and ends naturally drier than straighter hair types. During summer, UV exposure gradually weakens the hair's protective lipid layer, while humidity repeatedly swells and contracts the cuticle as moisture moves in and out of the strand. Over time, these stressors make curls less efficient at retaining moisture. The result: curls that once had defined, springy shape may become frizzier at the crown, drier through the lengths, and less responsive to the products and routines that usually work. Your Reset: Shampoo once this week — over-cleansing strips the little natural oil curly hair does produce. Use Curly Hair Conditioner generously, working through with fingers while wet. Mid-week, swap in the Curly Hair Mask for 10 minutes (mango butter and coconut oil work at a level a rinse-out conditioner can't match). Layer Curly Leave-In Treatment over damp hair before styling, then scrunch Super Shape Curl Cream for definition and frizz control. Coily Hair: Your Structure Needs Intentional Replenishment Coily hair has the most tightly coiled structure of any hair type, making it the most challenging for sebum to travel from the scalp to the ends. As a result, coily hair is naturally drier and relies more heavily on its protective lipid layer and external moisture to maintain softness and flexibility. During summer, UV exposure gradually degrades those surface lipids, while humidity causes repeated swelling and lifting of the cuticle, making it even harder for the hair to retain moisture. The result: hair may feel drier, rougher, and more fragile, with less stretch, more shrinkage, and increased breakage if moisture isn't consistently replenished. Your reset: Use the Custom Co-Wash to cleanse the scalp while delivering moisture to the lengths simultaneously. Follow with Coily Hair Conditioner, then seal with Coily Leave-In Treatment while hair is still soaking wet. Use the Coily Hair Mask twice this week in place of conditioner — murumuru butter nourishes deeply and reduces the surface friction that drives roughness. For coily hair specifically, the Custom Hair Serum (available through our quiz) is a worthwhile add as a final sealing step after your leave-in on days when your structure needs that extra moisture lock. The One Thing All Hair Types Have in Common Right Now Every hair type responds to summer the same way: the cuticle has been cycling through moisture and heat repeatedly for weeks, and it needs consistency. A single deep conditioning treatment won't undo two months of summer, but a reset week with the right products for your specific structure gets your hair behaving the way it did before summer. Your structure already knows what it needs. Now you do too.
articles.title: How Summer Changes Your Hair: A Hair Type Guide to Restoring Moisture and Shine

articles.summary: Summer doesn't just change how your hair looks and feels. It changes what's happening at the scalp. Sweat, sunscreen, extra time outdoors, and shifting wash schedules all affect your scalp first. How your scalp responds depends entirely on your hair type. The Science Behind Summer Scalp Care Every hair type has a different relationship with sebum, the natural oil your scalp produces. The shape of your hair fiber determines how easily that oil travels from root to end. During summer, heat, sweat, and sunscreen residue all interact with that process differently. Understanding your hair's structure is the difference between guessing at a routine and building one that works with your scalp instead. How to Remove Sunscreen, Sweat, and Build-up Sunscreen formulas are water-resistant and contain zinc oxide or waxes, so you may need to apply your hair type shampoo directly to your roots and let it sit for 2 to 3 minutes to thoroughly break down the residue. If you are still feeling like you have residue on your hair, repeat the shampoo and double cleanse. Double cleansing means shampooing your hair twice during the same wash. The first cleanse lifts away sweat, excess oil, sunscreen, and product buildup from the scalp. The second cleanse gives your scalp a deeper clean, allowing your shampoo to work more effectively and leaving your hair feeling fresher and more balanced. First Cleanse: Thoroughly wet your hair, then work a quarter-sized amount of shampoo between your palms before applying it to your scalp. Using your fingertips, gently massage for 30 to 60 seconds to loosen buildup and impurities. Rinse thoroughly. Second Cleanse: Apply a slightly smaller amount of shampoo to your scalp. Because the initial buildup has already been removed, you'll notice a richer lather. Continue massaging your scalp, allowing the lather to glide through the lengths of your hair as you rinse. Finish by rinsing until the water runs clear. Straight Hair: Managing Faster Oil Production Straight hair's flat, tightly aligned cuticle allows sebum to travel from root to tip with the least resistance of any hair type. That's one reason straight hair often looks naturally shiny. During summer, however, heat and increased perspiration can accelerate oil buildup, leaving the scalp feeling greasy sooner than usual. Double Wash with Straight Hair Shampoo to remove sweat and buildup without over-stripping the scalp. Double cleansing is highly beneficial for straight hair in the summer. Straight hair allows oils to travel easily from the scalp to the ends, causing it to look greasy faster, especially when combined with summer sweat, humidity, and sunscreen. The first wash breaks down buildup, and the second deeply cleanses your scalp. Follow with Straight Hair Conditioner to keep lengths soft without weighing down fine hair. If you're heat-styling to manage humidity, add a Custom Styling Primer to your routine. A custom styling primer is formulated with provitamin B5 that provides color, UV, and heat protection (up to 450°F), formulated for your unique hair goals with a personalized level of hold. Wavy Hair: Balancing Oily Roots and Dry Ends Wavy hair sits in the middle of the hair type spectrum. Oil can accumulate at the roots while the mid-lengths and ends remain dry. Summer sweat tends to collect at the scalp, which can flatten your wave pattern before the rest of your hair even feels affected. Cleanse with Wavy Hair Shampoo and follow with Wavy Hair Conditioner to balance moisture without weighing down your waves. For a midday or post-workout refresh, work a small amount of Zero Gravity Styling Mousse through damp roots. It helps reactivate wave definition without adding unnecessary buildup. Try the Zero Gravity Mousse here for 15% off with CODE: 15OFFMOUSSE Curly Hair: Preventing Layered Buildup Curly hair's bends slow the movement of sebum, so oily roots are rarely the biggest concern during summer. Buildup is. Sweat, sunscreen, and styling products can layer between wash days, leaving curls feeling coated instead of defined. Use Curly Hair Shampoo to lift away buildup, then follow with Curly Hair Conditioner to restore hydration and improve manageability. Between wash days, work a small amount of Super Shape Curl Cream through damp roots and lengths to refresh curl definition without needing a full wash. Coily Hair: Protecting the Scalp Between Washes Coily hair's tight coil pattern makes it the most difficult for sebum to travel from the scalp to the ends. That's why coily hair routines are often built around less frequent washing. During summer, however, longer intervals between washes allow sweat, sunscreen, and styling products to remain on the scalp longer. Coily Hair Shampoo is formulated to cleanse thoroughly without stripping away the moisture that coily hair depends on. Follow with Coily Hair Conditioner to restore softness and manageability. Maintaining your regular wash schedule, rather than extending time between washes to avoid dryness, helps keep your scalp healthy during the hottest months of the year. The Bottom Line Summer scalp care is about understanding how your hair's structure manages oil, sweat, and buildup, then building a routine that supports those needs. When you care for your scalp based on your hair type, you're creating the ideal foundation for hair that looks healthier, feels balanced, and performs at its best all season long.
